blocks.text: Anterior pituitary secretes many hormones, many of which regulate the activity of other endocrine glands.

items: Growth Hormone (GH, or somatotropin) stimulates the growth of muscles, bones (indirectly), and other tissues. It is also essential for proper metabolic regulation.
Adrenocorticotropic Hormone (ACTH, or corticotropin) stimulates the adrenal cortex for the secretion of corticosteroids (cortisone and aldosterone), which regulate glucose and salt homeostasis.

blocks.title: Tidbit
blocks.text:
Growth Hormone Treatment
GH treatment is given to children have short stature due to GH deficiency. It improves their growth rate.
However, every dwarf person does not have GH deficiency. So, GH therapy may not be appropriate for everyone.
Some people use GH because they believe it will build muscle or slow aging. However, doctors do not support the use of GH for these purposes.

items: Thyroid-stimulating Hormone (TSH, or thyrotropin) stimulates the thyroid gland to produce thyroxine, which in turn stimulates oxidative respiration.
Luteinizing Hormone (LH) In females, it stimulates ovaries to produce progesterone and estrogen hormones. It also initiates ovulation. In males, it stimulates testes for testosterone production.
Follicle-stimulating Hormone (FSH) stimulates the development of ovarian follicles in females. In males, it stimulated the development of sperms. FSH and LH are both referred to as gonadotropins.
Prolactin stimulates the mammary glands to produce milk. It is produced in both male and female but functions only in female.
